questions.question: How is the carrier signal used in the demodulation of a DSB-SC signal?

answers.a: The carrier signal is needed at the receiver to recover the original message signal.
answers.b: The carrier signal is not needed for demodulation; only the modulated signal is required.
answers.c: The carrier signal is used to filter out the sidebands.
answers.d: The carrier signal is used to amplify the modulated signal.

explanations.a: Correct! The carrier signal is essential for coherent detection of a DSB-SC signal to recover the original message.
explanations.b: Incorrect! The carrier is crucial for the demodulation process in DSB-SC.
explanations.c: Incorrect! The carrier signal is not used for filtering sidebands but for mixing.
explanations.d: Incorrect! Amplification is not the role of the carrier signal in demodulation.

questions.question: In Single Sideband Suppressed Carrier (SSB-SC) modulation, how is the message signal typically reconstructed?

answers.a: By mixing the received signal with a local oscillator that has the same frequency as the carrier used in modulation.
answers.b: By filtering out the unwanted sideband from the received signal.
answers.c: By using an envelope detector to extract the message signal.
answers.d: By direct demodulation without any further processing.

explanations.a: Correct! Reconstruction requires mixing with a local oscillator to retrieve the original message signal.
explanations.b: Incorrect! Filtering out the sideband is not sufficient; mixing is required.
explanations.c: Incorrect! Envelope detection is not suitable for SSB-SC as it requires coherent detection.
explanations.d: Incorrect! Direct demodulation is not feasible without additional processing in SSB-SC.

questions.question: In DSB-SC modulation, why is carrier phase synchronization important at the receiver?

answers.a: To ensure proper amplitude scaling of the message signal
answers.b: To correctly recover the message signal during coherent detection
answers.c: To eliminate noise from the received signal

explanations.a: Incorrect! Amplitude scaling is not the main reason.
explanations.b: Correct! Incorrect phase causes distortion or complete signal loss during demodulation.
explanations.c: Incorrect! Noise cannot be eliminated by phase synchronization.
explanations.d: Incorrect! Bandwidth is not affected by phase synchronization.

questions.question: In SSB-SC demodulation, what combination of operations is required to recover the message signal?

answers.c: Mixing with carrier followed by low-pass filtering

explanations.a: Incorrect! Envelope detection does not work for suppressed carrier signals.
explanations.b: Incorrect! Filtering alone cannot recover the baseband signal.
explanations.c: Correct! Coherent detection requires mixing followed by LPF.
explanations.d: Incorrect! High-pass filtering is not used for demodulation.

questions.question: In DSB-SC modulation, how is the amplitude of the carrier signal affected by the modulation process?

answers.a: The amplitude of the carrier signal is suppressed or removed.
answers.b: The amplitude of the carrier signal increases proportionally with the message signal.
answers.c: The amplitude of the carrier signal remains unchanged.
answers.d: The amplitude of the carrier signal is modulated in a manner similar to amplitude modulation.

explanations.a: Correct! In DSB-SC modulation, the carrier signal's amplitude is suppressed; only the sidebands carry the information.
explanations.b: Incorrect! The carrier amplitude does not increase; it is suppressed.
explanations.c: Incorrect! The carrier amplitude is not unchanged; it is suppressed.
explanations.d: Incorrect! The carrier is suppressed, not amplitude-modulated in DSB-SC.

questions.question: What is the key difference between DSB-SC and SSB-SC in terms of bandwidth usage?

answers.a: DSB-SC uses twice the bandwidth of SSB-SC.
answers.b: SSB-SC uses twice the bandwidth of DSB-SC.
answers.c: DSB-SC and SSB-SC use the same bandwidth.
answers.d: Bandwidth usage depends on the modulation index of the signal.

explanations.a: Correct! DSB-SC has twice the bandwidth of SSB-SC because it includes both sidebands.
explanations.b: Incorrect! SSB-SC is more bandwidth efficient and uses half the bandwidth of DSB-SC.
explanations.c: Incorrect! The bandwidth of DSB-SC is double that of SSB-SC.
explanations.d: Incorrect! The bandwidth difference is not dependent on the modulation index.

questions.question: In an SSB-SC signal, what happens to the carrier frequency?

answers.a: The carrier frequency is completely removed from the signal.
answers.b: The carrier frequency is present but at a reduced amplitude.
answers.c: The carrier frequency is modulated along with the message signal.
answers.d: The carrier frequency is used for phase modulation of the message signal.

explanations.a: Correct! The carrier is removed or suppressed in SSB-SC, leaving only one sideband.
explanations.b: Incorrect! The carrier is not present at a reduced amplitude; it is suppressed.
explanations.c: Incorrect! The carrier frequency is not transmitted in SSB-SC.
explanations.d: Incorrect! Phase modulation is not related to SSB-SC since the carrier is suppressed.

questions.question: What is the total bandwidth required to transmit a DSB-SC signal if the message signal has a maximum frequency of f_m?

explanations.a: Incorrect! DSB-SC includes both upper and lower sidebands, so the bandwidth is larger than f_m.
explanations.b: Correct! The total bandwidth of a DSB-SC signal is twice the maximum frequency of the message signal.
explanations.c: Incorrect! 4 f_m is too large; it would correspond to other modulation schemes or redundant duplication.
explanations.d: Incorrect! Half the message frequency is too small for DSB-SC.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains why SSB-SC is preferred over DSB-SC in long-distance communication systems?

answers.a: It uses less bandwidth and avoids transmitting redundant sideband power
answers.b: It eliminates the need for coherent detection
answers.c: It increases the carrier power for better transmission

explanations.a: Correct! SSB-SC transmits only one sideband, reducing bandwidth and saving power by eliminating redundant components.
explanations.b: Incorrect! SSB-SC still requires coherent detection.
explanations.c: Incorrect! The carrier is suppressed, not increased.
explanations.d: Incorrect! SSB-SC receivers are actually more complex.

questions.question: In a communication system using DSB-SC, what is the main reason a coherent detector is preferred over an envelope detector?

answers.a: Coherent detection accurately recovers the message signal even when the carrier is suppressed.
answers.b: Envelope detection is faster than coherent detection.
answers.c: Coherent detection requires less power than envelope detection.
answers.d: Envelope detection can recover SSB-SC signals reliably.

explanations.a: Correct! Since DSB-SC suppresses the carrier, envelope detection fails, and coherent detection using a locally generated carrier is required to correctly demodulate the signal.
explanations.b: Incorrect! Speed is not the main reason; coherent detection is needed for accuracy.
explanations.c: Incorrect! Coherent detection generally consumes more resources due to carrier synchronization.
explanations.d: Incorrect! Envelope detection cannot recover SSB-SC or DSB-SC signals.
